blocks.task_summary: Count six-digit positive integers with distinct digits chosen from 0–9, where the first digit cannot be zero.
method_path: Remaining 5 positions: arrange 5 from the 9 remaining digits (including 0): P(9,5) = 9 × 8 × 7 × 6 × 5

evidence.basis: Markscheme shows M1 for 9 × 9 × 8 × 7 × 6 × 5 or 9 × P(9,5); A1 for 136080 or 9 × 9!/4!. Notes award M1A0 for common errors 10_P_6 = 151200 and 9_P_6 = 60480.

blocks.task_summary: Count six-digit positive integers with distinct digits in strictly increasing order, chosen from digits 0–9.
method_path: Digits must be non-zero (0 cannot appear as first/smallest digit in an increasing six-digit number)
Each unordered selection yields exactly one increasing arrangement
accepted_alternatives: C(9,3) = 84 (remove 3 digits from 9 non-zero digits; remaining 6 have exactly one increasing arrangement)

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: every unordered subset of 6 digits from the set of 9 non-zero digits can be arranged in exactly one way into a 6-digit number with the digits in increasing order. C(9,6) × 1. Answer 84. METHOD 2: removes 3 digits from the set of 9 non-zero digits and these 6 remaining digits can be arranged in exactly one way. C(9,3) × 1. Answer 84.
